Reentrancy is proven; the extraction arithmetic is not. Stage 2 must model the balance check and show a positive attacker delta. If the check uses a stored reserve updated before the callback, this collapses to DoS.

Mechanism is only an excerpt; the exact accounting that lets a malicious-market receipt draw on a legitimate pool needs Stage 2. Potential is high (insurance pool drain) but unproven. Do not count the full pool until the receipt/claim math is read.

The double-mint is clear, but custom token registration is admin-gated; the attack needs an already-registered callback token. That gate is why this is medium, not high. Stage 2: enumerate registered ERC777/callback tokens on the Arbitrum bridge and check whether the deployed gateway predates the reentrancy guard.

Explicit PoC with an over-refund and a predicted vault shortage. The gain is the platform fee (5% in the test), so it scales with contribution size. Stage 2: confirm the deployed program records gross and that refunds are paid from the shared vault.

The report explicitly says 'steals the closing fee from the diamond, creating a drain over time'. Per-trade value is small (a fee), so the profit depends on repetition and on forcing the negative-collateral branch. Stage 2: read the branch condition and whether a trader can make it true without a loss.

The hijack is proven, but the value depends on what a referral score is worth. If scores are only a leaderboard, this is UNECONOMIC. Stage 2: read the reward distribution that consumes scoreOf and confirm it pays tokens.

Real double-pay but entirely off-chain orchestration; the on-chain transfer is a normal USDC payment, so Stage 2 fork-testing cannot reproduce it without the backend. Value is capped by the promo amount. Low priority for an on-chain profit hunt.

The accounting corruption is clear; the profit is a liquidator bonus on a healthy position, which requires the corrupted value to flip the health check. Stage 2: model the sign/magnitude and check whether the attacker can be both the position owner and the liquidator (self-liquidation is usually blocked or unprofitable).

Profit is real-world goods/services, not on-chain funds, and depends on backend sequencing. The report itself rates impact indeterminate. Low priority for an on-chain fork test; useful only as an operational-risk note.

The unsaved-pool bug is clear; the exact profit depends on which leg settles before the break. Stage 2: trace the message handler to see whether tokens/NFTs move before pools_to_save is skipped. If both legs revert on failure, this is only a stale-price DoS.

The missing check is clear; the profit depends on the consumer and on the oracle actually being stale. Stage 2: read the call sites of custody_aum and whether the Doves feed's timestamp is validated upstream by Jupiter. If the client's claim is true, this is mitigated.

Stage 2: confirm the liquidation bonus is paid to the caller and that the confidence adjustment can actually cross the liquidation threshold for a position that is healthy at mid price. Primary impact is revert/griefing. The 'withdraw more than intended' branch is an early-exit at an inflated NAV, which is value preservation rather than extraction; a Stage 2 fork test would need to show the exiting LP receives more than their pro-rata claim.

Clear value leak to incumbent holders, but not an attacker-initiated profit: depositing yourself loses money and redeeming your own shares is fair. The report itself frames it as new depositors receiving fewer shares. Classified DOS_ONLY as economic griefing; revisit only if Stage 2 finds a way to force deposits.
Owner loss / frozen NFT. No attacker value capture. A third party might later buy the stranded NFT if the contract exposes it, but the report does not describe such a path.
Pure DoS/griefing. The reentrancy gives the attacker no extra assets: each iteration returns the same NFT. Stage 2 should not spend time fork-testing this for profit.
Operational fund freeze; the PoC is a model, not the production code. No attacker payout. If Stage 2 finds an admin unlock path that pays the caller, revisit.
Liveness/fund-stuck bug. A miner or reorg cannot profit from an invalid signature. Fixed by per-input BIP341 signing.

Redemption freeze. The only 'beneficiary' is the protocol (it keeps assets), not an external attacker. Could become a bank-run advantage for the last withdrawer, but the report does not describe that.

Griefing with borrower loss. Unless the caller is the lender and the early close improves their recovery, there is no attacker payout. Stage 2 should check whether the caller can be a liquidator-like beneficiary.

Accounting/liveness defect. The missing fee is a protocol loss, not an attacker gain. Stage 2 should check whether any permissionless function can withdraw the storage contract's balance; if so, this flips to PROFIT_PLAUSIBLE.

Escape-from-liquidation / bad-debt risk. The gain is avoided loss, not extracted value. It could become profit if the user withdraws more collateral than their equity, but the report does not show that. NEAR async makes the race real.
Permanent redemption DoS. The stuck value belongs to the affected controller, not the attacker. Not a profit candidate.

Bank-run/insolvency, not value minted to the attacker. The fee dodge is a cost saving. To become profit, Stage 2 would need to show the exiting LP's assets exceed their fair share after marking the tranche to market.

Griefing/freezing of the victim's allowance. The report says deposit() is used by game contracts to handle player deposits; if the game credits the caller as the depositor, this becomes theft. The body does not show that. Stage 2: read the game-side accounting before counting it.

The report explicitly says there is 'no direct way to utilize more bribe rewards'. This is griefing/dilution, not profit. Unless the attacker is a candidate who benefits from a lower payout to voters, it is DOS_ONLY.

Griefing/dilution; the attacker pays the donated SY and gets no direct payout. If the stranded rewards can later be swept by the attacker, it flips. Stage 2: check for a permissionless sweep of the yield-token contract balance.
Self-harm bug: the caller is the victim. An attacker cannot make another user call repay. Not a profit candidate.

Primarily user loss and broken liquidation. The 'unliquidatable borrow' variant is a bad-debt risk, not a demonstrated drain. Stage 2 would need a live market and a borrower who can stake and then default.
Reward-distribution liveness bug. Unless the skipped lamports can be permissionlessly swept to the caller, there is no attacker profit. Fixed by resetting the index.
Liveness/accounting break. The only actor who can close a market is the owner, so this is also partly privileged-triggered. Not a profit candidate.

Griefing/unauthorized lifecycle action. If the caller can name themselves as the foreclosure beneficiary, it becomes profit; the body does not say. Stage 2: read the payout recipient in the blueprint before counting it.

Fund freeze for the offeror. Unless the stranded tokens can be claimed by another offer, there is no attacker payout. Stage 2: check whether the deleted offer's funds become claimable by a subsequent taker.
Revenue loss, not theft. The LayerZero Deployer is a protocol contract, not an attacker. Unless someone can upgrade the Deployer to add receive(), there is no capture.

Insolvency/liveness bug. An early winner can be paid while later winners are not, but that is not a profit over fair odds. Stage 2 would need a way to force multiple games to win in the same window (e.g. manipulate randomness); the report does not provide one.

Title-level classification only: locked fees are a loss to LPs, not a transfer to an attacker. If the locked fees can be swept by a later caller, this changes. Stage 2 needs the PDF (LimitBreak Round Two, H-01, pages 19-21).
Revenue loss; the redeemer pays the same USDV. No attacker capture. The discussion thread is about fix correctness, not exploitability. Not a Stage 2 profit target.
Revenue loss, not theft. The shortfall variant creates unbacked supply, which is an insolvency risk, not an attacker payout. Stage 2 should not fork-test this for profit.

Ceremony sabotage/quorum manipulation, not an on-chain EOA profit. The 'loss of funds' impact is speculative (placeholder keys are generated in the code). Stage 2 is not applicable unless a key-compromise path is demonstrated.

Real accounting bug, but the attacker benefit is fee avoidance only, and the underflow variant is a DoS on fee collection. Not worth a Stage 2 fork test unless the fee is the dominant PnL of the vault.

Fee avoidance, not theft. The maximum gain is the fee on the user's own deposit. Not worth a fork test unless the fee is the protocol's main revenue and the report's 'High' impact is being used for prioritisation.

Early unlock of one's own principal. The gain is the time value of the lock (e.g. airdrop eligibility), not a transfer from other users. Not a profit target unless the lock gates a valuable airdrop; then the profit is the airdrop, not the LP.
Fee avoidance / griefing of the fee recipient. The cost (gas + capital) likely exceeds the saved fee for small positions. Not a profit target unless the strategy is huge and the fee is large.

The cap bypass is real, but every token is fully paid for at the protocol's own price. That is a dilution/scarcity attack, not a transfer of protocol funds. If the mint price is far below market, the gain is normal mint arbitrage; count it only if Stage 2 finds the item is sold at a fixed price with no per-wallet limit and the floor is materially higher.

Fee bypass with the attacker's own capital. The client's response says launches are gated by a backend signature, which also weakens the unprivileged case. Not a profit target unless the launch fee is the protocol's main revenue and the gate is bypassable.
Fee avoidance only, and the saving is a fraction of the withdrawal fee. Gas on the target chain may eat the gain for small amounts. Not a Stage 2 priority.

The over-refund is real but bounded by maxRefundAmount and by the gas actually spent; the executor is out of pocket for gas first. The net gain is at most the duplicated gas cost, which is small. Fixed with nonReentrant. Not worth a Stage 2 fork test.

Privilege escalation within an already-privileged role. No unprivileged path. Fixed by removing shareRegistrarRole. Not a Stage 2 profit target unless a key compromise is in scope.

Real profit, but gated by the lender role and KYC; it is a counterparty abusing a refinance privilege, not an unprivileged EOA. If Stage 2 shows anyone can become a lender without KYC and the borrower is auto-bound to a replacement offer, reclassify as PROFIT_PLAUSIBLE.

Governance cannot revoke a malicious privileged feeder. The attacker already holds the feeder role, so this is PRIVILEGED. No unprivileged path. If a feeder key is compromised, the impact is price manipulation, but that is a key-compromise scenario.

Real theft, but the caller is the privileged rebalancer. No unprivileged path. Fixed by deriving the mint from vault_token_destination. If Stage 2 finds execute_rebalancing is permissionless, reclassify.

PoC shows owner 0x7c8999... becoming 0x328809... (alice). The report's phrasing about 'contract owns an NFT' is loose; Stage 2 must confirm _transfer's ownership bypass for from==to==address(this).
Real reentrancy across the recipe boundary, but it needs the victim to route through an attacker contract. Profit is whatever the victim's proxy holds/approves. HF excerpt only; no PoC.

The report's HF entry has a PoC function list (HackToken, transferManager) and states the check is 'caller is an agent for a traded token' rather than 'second participant or treasury agent'. Profit = victim's approved balance.
Admin/role key risk, not an external attack. Would become profitable only with a compromised privileged key.
Mechanism in the excerpt is complete, but the corpus title carries 'Project self-injected exploit', so code reality is unverified. Treat as a lead, not a confirmed live bug.

PoC shows a random user removing a selector. If the deployed diamond has an owner check or is still uninitialised, exploitability changes; Stage 2 must check the deployed proxy. Also enables DoS by removing selectors.
The gate is asset listing, a privileged/config decision. Report itself rates likelihood Low for this reason.
Acknowledged as unreachable in the deployed instruction ordering; at most a small LP mispricing.
Role-gated. The report's concern is role hygiene (a non-staking minter), not an unprivileged path.
Griefing/fairness bug. The only 'gain' is avoiding a loss, which is not attacker profit under the classification; no funds move to the caller.

project: PoolTogether - Sushi and Yearn V2 Yield Sources
target_project: PoolTogether - Sushi and Yearn V2 Yield Sources
notes: Real reentrancy pattern but not reachable with the plain ERC-20 assets actually used; no identified hook token in this deployment. 2021 finding, likely long fixed.
Single-variable typo with catastrophic accounting effect; report says any staking user can withdraw as if owning all shares. Acknowledged, so verify the deployed version still has the typo.
Rewards stranded; griefing/accounting, not profit.
Launch-condition bug with no explicit attacker payout. Could be a buy-side advantage or a broken pool, but that is speculation; kept UNCLEAR.
Wrong-asset transfer causes stuck funds for users; the only caller is a privileged role, so no external profit.
Overpayment is a share of the premium pool, not principal. Profit is bounded by the premium and by the attacker's fixed deposit; timing-dependent.
Report PoC shows bob's stETH balance going 0 -> 50e18. Two variants: residual allowance, or front-running the approval. Fixed by requiring benefactor == msg.sender (5afc1851).

Arbitrary-amount transfer from the hub's own balance; no victim action needed. Fixed in f6fa8cd1 by checking the Uniswap V3 factory. The duplicate finding (78) is the same bug from the electisec report.
HF excerpt only; the mechanism is specific (entire requested amount becomes the frontend fee). Stage 2 must read fillLPOrder to confirm the fee assignment and whether self-fill is allowed.
Design/accounting issue; the gain would be a share-price delta that also affects the attacker's own position. No concrete profit path.
Acknowledged, not fixed. Profit depends on the PT discount and on borrow limits; the report does not quantify. Treat as an oracle-mispricing lead.
Profit equals whatever the proposal transfers; the report notes the council reviews proposals, which may block execution. Needs a concrete proposal payload to be a real theft.
Report gives a step-by-step PoC. Profit is bounded only by the reward pool, so this is a full drain of emissions. Fixed in #437db43 by requiring toCheckpoint >= lastProcessedCheckpoint.
Functional DoS only; resolved in PR #60.
Funds stranded, no attacker payout. Unless the facet has a sweep function, this is pure loss/DoS.
A race rather than a deterministic exploit; profit = other in-flight deposits. Report cross-references C-02 (same root cause). Verify ordering rules in Stage 2.
Title-level DoS only. Do not infer more without the report.
Report explicitly says Bob can end up with all voting power and all rewards. Profit is the reward pool, but the CBR manipulation and reward accounting need a fork test.
Owner-privileged accounting bug; not reachable by an external EOA.
Cross-user transient-storage poisoning; the report says the attacker 'can take all the tokens and return nothing'. Profit depends on finding a victim contract whose redeem is permissionless. Fixed.
Title-level only. Fixed per status. Stage 2 would need the deployed ABI/source to confirm; do not promote without it.
Funds go to deposit.owner, so the attacker must be the depositor; that is easy (deposit, force failure). Profit = repeat withdrawals up to localPort balance. Fixed in a0dd0311.
Report says it 'allows the attacker to steal an unlimited amount of funds'. Fixed in efb4dcd2 by checking the current collateral in the callback. Requires a live trader flow and keeper ordering.
Attacker pays the offer price, so profit = punk market value minus that price. If the owner sets the sale price to the pool's intended deposit value (often 0), the attacker gets it nearly free.
Report says 'infinite profit for themselves and an infinite loss for the liquidated user'. Fixed by 689db8b3 (issue 6.1). Profit = collateral minus debt repaid.
Missing distribution = stuck rewards, no profit. Body truncated.
Missing: whether an unprivileged user can trigger the withdrawal in the stale window and capture the delta. Body truncated.
Griefing/DoS; report title says 'causing user rewards to be stuck'. No profit.
Pure allowance theft with no capital. Fixed by removing the `from` parameter. The same pattern exists on unstake.
Counterparty-role abuse, not an unprivileged EOA. Body is a one-line note; mechanism under-specified.
Griefing by overfunding; attacker loses the dust it sends. No profit.
Accounting correctness issue; no profit path in the available text.
Report gives numeric Scenario 1 (Alice nets the victim's deposit). The gift is recovered on withdrawal, so net cost is gas plus price exposure. Resolved in fix #2.
PoC steals 100,000 NFTs in one call by passing the owner as `by`. Fixed by removing the override. This is one of the cleanest theft primitives in the batch.
Timing/accounting issue; profit would be a share-price arbitrage that also affects the attacker's own deposit. No concrete path.
The extra precondition is the weak point: the report asserts it is reachable from other findings. Stage 2 must confirm on the deployed program. Profit = LP redemption against real vault assets.
Direct prize theft, but the prize size is not stated. Fixed in a74bb3a1/9bd8af56. Note the inversion may let many non-winners claim, which would drain the pool faster.
Real accounting bug, but the extractable delta is a few percent of a small undeployed balance, and the main effect is the last claimant losing out. Not worth Stage 2.
Missing: how the spoofed fee/state converts into attacker balance. Resolved in 5275b76.
Duplicate of 46 from a second audit; same fix. Count once for Stage 2 but both confirm the bug was real and acknowledged.
The report's own constraints show the attacker sets itself as owner, so this is griefing/state pollution rather than theft.
PoC mints 50,000,000,000,000 units to an attacker ATA with no signer. Profit = whatever liquidity the token has; if GORPLES is only used inside the IDO, value depends on that. Fixed in 1df65f7f.

Report has a Foundry PoC. Net profit = LP value minus fee, i.e. the attacker gets leverage/deposit for free; the vault is not immediately short because the tokens return, but the attacker's claim on the pool is unearned. Fixed in 8ac545e7.
Identity/KYC bypass only; no profit mechanism. Report itself is tentative.
Profit depends on the size of the stale-price gap and on exit liquidity. Not a deterministic bug; more of a liveness/oracle-lag arbitrage.
Same class as Bunni (46/78). The HF excerpt is short; Stage 2 needs the adapter source to confirm the transfer direction and whether the callback is public.
Profit is funding/insurance-pool value; needs a fork test of the funding formula and market depth. No numbers in the excerpt.
Repeat-claim bug but gated by the front-end owner role; not an external EOA.
No pool to drain; the gain is the price difference on one purchase, and the direction depends on configuration. Dust.

Spot-quoter oracle is a well-known profit primitive; the HF entry lists a manipulation PoC function set. Profit = borrow minus collateral, capped by pool liquidity. Stage 2 must confirm the deployed quoter wiring.

Classic fake-pool reward inflation. Profit is the reward share taken from honest stakers; the worthless tokens cost nothing. Stage 2 should confirm how liquidity is measured and whether the pool must be factory-created.
Griefing/DoS of reward accounting; the attacker pays the cheap token and gets nothing back.
Profit is the over-credit, which is bounded by the pending payout amount; likely small and shared among early exiters. Needs a fork test.
Cross-chain forgery of the Bridge's own signal; the report says it steals ETH from the Bridge or tokens from vaults. Profit = bridge/vault balance, capped by what the forged message can move. Fixed.
Identity-management privilege issue; no direct fund pool. Fixed.
Whitelist/compliance bypass with consenting owner; no attacker gain beyond access. High severity for the protocol, not profit.

Report is truncated at 'draining or locking...', so the final extraction step is not fully shown. Still, permissionless pull from a shared reward wallet is a credible drain. Stage 2 must read createMarketV2 and the market payout logic.
Do not infer. Same report as finding 2; both bodies are withheld.
Parameter/design issue acknowledged without fix; the arbitrage is thin and requires capital to move TVL. Not a Stage 2 priority.
Reward insolvency/DoS; resolved per title.
Privileged-key/governance risk; no external EOA path.
Blocks future position opening; no funds move to the caller.
Silent failure/loss, not profit. Body truncated.
Missing: a concrete replay that pays the attacker. The signers are privileged, so this is closer to a double-distribution risk than an unprivileged theft.
Rounding-dust class; acknowledged. Not economically extractable at scale.
Fee avoidance, not fund extraction; the amount is a per-delivery fee. Client accepted it as a tradeoff.
Report says 'might cause' and was fixed in V2. Profit = payer's token balance in that flow; Stage 2 must confirm the deployed instruction set and signer layout.

The report explicitly says 'clear path for profitable arbitrage in outer contracts', but the audited contract was removed from scope. Profit depends on a consumer; Stage 2 would need the consumer list.
Report gives the exact numbers (100 proUSD -> $103 of yAsset). Profit is the premium above the cap per redemption; repeatable while the yAsset trades above cap. Fixed in 93f8bfa (max instead of min).
Status 'Not Applicable' in the report, and no consumer is named. Kept low-confidence; would need the adapter's users to be profitable.
Arithmetic underflow causing failed calls; no value transfer.
Migration griefing; tokens stuck rather than stolen.

cancelAuction with zero bids deducts initiatorFee from reservePrice and repays liens only partially, leaving debt and liens in place so release checks keep failing and the NFT stays locked. [report status: open]

_depositAndRepayMorphoFlashLoan and _redeemAndRepayMorphoFlashLoan execute arbitrary swapCalls, so a caller can include a transferFrom pulling a user's approved tokens to an attacker address. [report status: fixed]
repay transfers the full creditToYield to protocolFeeReceiver instead of only the fee, overcharging the user; the excess goes to the fee receiver. [report status: open]

queueWithdrawals accepts a user-supplied depositShares; a near-max value underflows the int256 subtraction to a huge positive balance, inflating the staker's shares without backing ETH. [report status: open]

_increaseLiquidity/_increaseLiquidityFromManager are public and unrestricted, so an attacker passes their own tokenId and the contract adds protocol funds to the attacker-owned Uniswap V3 position. [report status: fixed]
Owner-controlled fee setters can raise protocol/subject/referral fees to 100% with no cap or grace period; owner-only. [report status: fixed]
The bridge charged 2.5% instead of the documented 0.3% and no ERC721 fee; users are overcharged, the excess goes to the protocol. [report status: fixed]
withdrawRequest updates basketRequestsSum without locking or burning tokens, so an attacker can inflate sell pressure and corrupt the basket accounting. [report status: fixed]
depositEth/depositWeth with PredefinedPool.sDAI does not convert to DAI first, so a user can receive ~1 DAI per ETH; the loss falls on the depositor. [report status: fixed]

distributeRewards mints pro-rata to current totalSupply without a duration weight, so a whale can stake just before distribution, unstake after, and capture a disproportionate share of rewards. [report status: fixed]
calculateCoverCost mixes per-second and per-day units, so a membership top-up is heavily undercharged and the user obtains coverage for far less than the intended premium. [report status: fixed]
If all stakers redeem and totalSupply becomes zero during an auction, returnFunds divides by zero and the auction cannot complete, trapping underlying. [report status: open]

Minting validations compare incoming amounts against the DAO's current token balance rather than total raised, so caps can be bypassed. The excerpt does not state what the bypassed cap lets the caller obtain. [report status: open]
Keeper rewards are not scaled to the settlement token's decimals, so keepers are overpaid; keeper is a permissioned role. [report status: open]

Deposit liquidity is derived from token_max_a at the current spot price, so an attacker can sandwich the deposit and force the depositor to provide mostly token A for far less LP than intended. [report status: open]
